messages:
sam_dx: hitting a handful of support tickets where `pip install git+https://github.com/redwood/repo.git@main` errors with `Could not build wheels for redwood-sdk`. User is on macOS arm, Python 3.11.

lee_engineer: that error usually points at pyproject/build-backend mismatch or missing wheel metadata. Are we still using poetry-core only?

mika_pkg: yep: pyproject uses `poetry-core` and we rely on poetry for release builds. Direct VCS pip installs are sensitive to pip/build versions. Also noticed we didn't include `py.typed` in the package, so typing consumers get nothing.

tanya_support: user also complained that after install `from redwood import AsyncClient` fails. Works in dev when installing editable.

ci-bot: Packaging test failed in CI job packaging/pr-1357: wheel build stage errored on macos-12-arm64. Link: https://ci.internal/job/1357/logs

lee_engineer: editable installs point at source tree which masks missing exports in `__init__.py`. We should export AsyncClient there. Quick patch: `from .client import Client\nfrom .async_client import AsyncClient\n__all__ = ["Client","AsyncClient"]`.

mika_pkg: packaging checklist: 1) ensure `py.typed` shipped (MANIFEST.in or pyproject include), 2) explicit exports in `__init__.py`, 3) consider switching build-system to setuptools+wheel for better pip-from-vcs compatibility or document pip>=23 requirement.

sam_dx: for immediate workaround what do we tell users?

tanya_support: suggested workaround: upgrade pip & tooling, then build wheel locally: `python -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel build` then `python -m build` and `pip install dist/*.whl`. For poetry users: `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes -o reqs.txt && pip install -r reqs.txt`. I'll send that in the ticket.

lee_engineer: long-term we should add cibuildwheel to produce manylinux/macos universal2 wheels so pip won't need to compile on consumer machines. Also add a CI smoke test that does `pip install dist/*.whl` in a clean venv and runs `python -c "from redwood import AsyncClient; import pkgutil; print(pkgutil.get_data('redwood','py.typed') is not None)"`.

mika_pkg: small PR to fix now: update pyproject.build-system to setuptools+wheel, add `redwood/py.typed` to include, add exports to `__init__.py`, and add `tests/test_package_imports.py` which does simple import from installed wheel. I'll open it shortly.

ci-bot: PR #1357 created with packaging fixes. Manual re-run queued.

sam_dx: awesome — once CI green can we publish a patch wheel and ping the affected users?

tanya_support: yes I'll prepare release notes and KB with the pip/poetry commands and the tip about older pip versions. :thumbsup:

lee_engineer: FYI also check for dependencies that trigger local C builds (eg libc-based libs). If we have any optional C deps we should mark them extras or vendor prebuilt wheels. Otherwise users on arm will hit compile failures.

mika_pkg: noted. I'll audit requirements.txt and bump any heavy native deps to optional/extras.

sam_dx: thanks all. Keep the fixes minimal and documented so onboarding friction reduces.
